steps.question: What should control corners say?
steps.why: Rounded by default; each brand sets its own corner.
Labels stay readable in every brand.
Customers are often on phones.
Each brand sets its own corner through the theme.

steps.pick: size.44
space.16

radius.4: We use a 4px corner for Aster's buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls in a calm, precise tone, by brand convention. A small radius does this by softening the edge just enough while the sides stay straight. So Aster feels exact and steady, the least round of the three brands, because each brand sets its corners (shape.values) on a neutral base (brand.q1).
neutral.600: the quietest text that still reads, 7.02:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.400: the quietest text that still reads, 6.97:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.

steps.question: What rises above the page?
steps.why: Cards lift slightly to group offers.

steps.question: How soft are shadows?
steps.why: Soft shadows fit every brand.
The shadow shows a menu or dialog floats above the page. Without it, it blends into the cards.

steps.pick: neutral.0, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge and its one shadow, not by its fill.
steps.darkPick: neutral.50, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge and its one shadow, not by its fill, as in light.

steps.pick: shadow.overlay: We use step 2 of the shadow scale for menus and dialogs in order to show floating height, one step above the cards. The cast shade does this by a 12px offset and a 32px blur at 16%, four times the card's blur. So a menu floats clear above the cards in every brand, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and shadows are soft (elevation.values).
steps.darkPick: shadow.overlay-dark: We use the light overlay shadow's shape in dark in order to show the same floating height by the dark-shade relation. The cast shade does this by the same 12px offset and 32px blur, at 50% black instead of 16%. So a menu still floats above the cards, though its shade reads weaker on dark than in light, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and dark ships for every brand (theming.values).

steps.pick: radius.8: We use an 8px corner for Aster's cards and dialogs in order to make each card read as a separate object, in a calm tone by brand convention. A modest radius does this by breaking the outline with a curve twice the 4px control corner. So a plan card reads as one object without feeling soft, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and each brand colors a neutral base (brand.q1).

steps.rule: Quiet edges and dividers. Decorative, so it has no contrast minimum.
steps.pick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.18:1, on surface.canvas). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.
steps.darkPick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.72:1, on surface.default). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.

steps.rule: The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surface it sits on: darker in light, lighter in dark.
steps.pick: neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.
steps.darkPick: neutral.100, one step lighter than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.50), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band on the menu and on cards.
